busy: Reading the address from its chain's indexer. A busy address takes a little while.
checked: Checked: whether the address itself is flagged, dealings with labelled exchanges, flagged addresses and mixers, use of the same address on several EVM chains, who sent the address its first coins on each chain, public names (ENS, Basenames, .sol), and for your own wallets, exchange deposit addresses they share with your other wallets. Flagged means a scam, a hack, OFAC's sanctions lists or a freeze by Tether or Circle. Only addresses in the label sets can be recognised, so no finding is not a clean bill.
empty: No address to scan. Paste an EVM, Solana or Tron address into the scanner.
error.title: The scan did not finish
evidence.title: What the findings rest on
finding.x-address-reuse.description_one: {{count}} address of this wallet was paid in more than one transaction. Anyone can see that those payments, and whatever the address spends, belong to one person.
finding.x-address-reuse.description_othe: {{count}} addresses of this wallet were paid in more than one transaction. Anyone can see that the payments to each of them, and whatever it spends, belong to one person.
finding.x-address-reuse.recommendation: Receive every payment on a fresh address: your wallet makes a new one whenever you ask. Here each reused address costs 10 points, at most 40; the deep scan of that one address grades it much lower.
finding.x-address-reuse.title: Reused addresses: {{count}}
finding.x-deposit-address-shared.descrip: This address and {{count}} other wallet of yours ({{wallets}}) paid the same {{exchange}} deposit address. A deposit address belongs to one exchange account, so anyone watching the chain can tell these wallets have one owner, and the exchange knows who. The address is recognised by how it behaves (it sends everything to {{exchange}} and has few senders): a strong guess, 85% sure, not a fact.

This address and {{count}} other wallets of yours ({{wallets}}) paid the same {{exchange}} deposit address. A deposit address belongs to one exchange account, so anyone watching the chain can tell these wallets have one owner, and the exchange knows who. The address is recognised by how it behaves (it sends everything to {{exchange}} and has few senders): a strong guess, 85% sure, not a fact.
finding.x-deposit-address-shared.recomme: Treat these wallets as one from now on: the link cannot be undone. To keep wallets apart, give each its own exchange account, or deposit only from a wallet that is already tied to that account.
finding.x-deposit-address-shared.title: Shares a {{exchange}} deposit address with {{wallets}}
finding.x-exchange-exposure.description_: {{count}} transfer went between this address and {{exchange}} on {{chains}}. The exchange knows that this address belongs to one of its customers, and can be made to say who.
{{count}} transfers went between this address and {{exchange}} on {{chains}}. The exchange knows that this address belongs to one of its customers, and can be made to say who.
finding.x-exchange-exposure.recommendati: Treat this address as known to the exchange. Keep funds that should stay apart from your identity away from it, and withdraw to a fresh address rather than to this one again.
finding.x-exchange-exposure.title: Dealt directly with an exchange: {{exchange}}
finding.x-flagged-address.description: A label set names this address as a scam, a hack, under sanctions (OFAC's lists) or frozen by Tether or Circle. Money sent to it can be lost or break sanctions law, and exchanges refuse or freeze funds that come from it.
finding.x-flagged-address.recommendation: Do not send money to it. If funds from it reached you, keep them apart from the rest and be ready to explain where they came from if an exchange asks.
finding.x-flagged-address.title: This address is flagged: {{name}}
finding.x-flagged-counterparty.descripti: {{count}} transfer with an address labelled as a scam, a hack, under sanctions or frozen by Tether or Circle. Exchanges can freeze or question funds that touched such an address.
{{count}} transfers with addresses labelled as a scam, a hack, under sanctions or frozen by Tether or Circle. Exchanges can freeze or question funds that touched such an address.
finding.x-flagged-counterparty.recommend: Keep these funds apart from the rest, and be ready to explain where they came from if an exchange asks.
finding.x-flagged-counterparty.title: Dealt with a flagged address: {{name}}
finding.x-funder-exchange.description: {{exchange}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}, the gas it started with. The exchange knows that this address belongs to one of its customers, and can be made to say who; anyone who looks at its first transaction sees the withdrawal too.
finding.x-funder-exchange.recommendation: Treat this address as known to the exchange from its first transaction. A wallet that should stay apart from your identity should not get its first coins straight from an exchange withdrawal.
finding.x-funder-exchange.title: First funded by an exchange: {{exchange}}
finding.x-funder-hub.description: {{funder}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}, and also sent coins to {{wallets}}. It is too busy to be one person, or known as a service: most likely an exchange or a payout service. So it is not taken as a link between your wallets; it still knows where it sent the coins.
finding.x-funder-hub.recommendation: If you know who it is, label it in the app. If it is an exchange, the exchange knows that both wallets belong to its customers.
finding.x-funder-hub.title: First funded by a busy address that also funded {{wallets}}
finding.x-funder-mine.description: Your wallet {{funder}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}. Anyone who looks at its first transaction ties the two together, and whatever is known about one then applies to the other.
finding.x-funder-mine.recommendation: Fund a wallet you want kept apart from your others from a source that does not lead back to them.
finding.x-funder-mine.title: First funded by your wallet {{funder}}
finding.x-funder-shared.description: {{funder}} sent this address its first coins on {{chains}}, and also sent coins to {{wallets}}, which you track as yours. It was read and is not busy, so it looks like one person: wallets funded by the same person are the first thing a Sybil hunter groups together.
finding.x-funder-shared.recommendation: If this address is a service you know, label it in the app. Otherwise treat these wallets as tied together, and fund the next one from a different source.
finding.x-funder-shared.title: Funded by the same address as {{wallets}}
finding.x-linked-public.description: This wallet can be tied to your public wallet {{wallet}} with {{confidence}}% confidence. Whoever knows that the public one is yours can follow the link to this one.
finding.x-linked-public.recommendation: See how under “Can it be tied to your other wallets?”. Funds that must stay private need a wallet that never deals with this one or with the public one.
finding.x-linked-public.title: Tied to your public wallet {{wallet}} ({{confidence}}%)
finding.x-mixer-counterparty.description: {{count}} transfer with a labelled mixer. Its use is public, and exchanges often flag funds that passed through a mixer.
{{count}} transfers with a labelled mixer. Its use is public, and exchanges often flag funds that passed through a mixer.
finding.x-mixer-counterparty.recommendat: Expect questions when these funds reach an exchange. A mixer only hides the path when its deposit and withdrawal cannot be matched, by amount or by timing.
finding.x-mixer-counterparty.title: Dealt with a mixer: {{name}}
finding.x-mixer-linked.description_one: This address and {{wallets}}, which you track as yours, used Tornado Cash's {{pool}} pool: one deposited and the other withdrew, with only {{count}} other deposit made in between. Anyone watching the pool sees how few deposits the withdrawal can have come from, so it ties the two together: the tracker counts that as a guess of {{confidence}}%, never more than 30%, since older deposits not yet withdrawn hide it a little more.
finding.x-mixer-linked.description_other: This address and {{wallets}}, which you track as yours, used Tornado Cash's {{pool}} pool: one deposited and the other withdrew, with only {{count}} other deposits made in between. Anyone watching the pool sees how few deposits the withdrawal can have come from, so it ties the two together: the tracker counts that as a guess of {{confidence}}%, never more than 30%, since older deposits not yet withdrawn hide it a little more.
finding.x-mixer-linked.recommendation: Wait until many others have deposited before you withdraw: from 20 deposits in between, this check no longer ties the two. The withdrawal already on chain cannot be undone, so treat these wallets as tied.
finding.x-mixer-linked.title: The mixer hides little: tied to {{wallets}}
finding.x-multi-chain.description: This address is active on {{chains}}. Whatever ties it to a person on one of them ties it on all of them.
finding.x-multi-chain.recommendation: Use a separate address on each chain whose activity you want kept apart.
finding.x-multi-chain.title: The same address on several chains
finding.x-name-addresses.description_one: {{name}} lists {{count}} address on {{chains}}: {{addresses}}. Anyone who looks the name up ties that address to this one.
finding.x-name-addresses.description_oth: {{name}} lists {{count}} addresses on {{chains}}: {{addresses}}. Anyone who looks the name up ties them to this address, and to each other.
finding.x-name-addresses.recommendation: Remove from the name's records every address you want kept apart from this one. A record removed now still shows in the name's history.
finding.x-name-addresses.title: Its name lists addresses on other chains
finding.x-name-record.description: This address has the public name {{name}}, which explorers and wallets show next to every one of its transactions. Whatever the name tells about you is tied to all of them.
finding.x-name-record.recommendation: If this address should not be tied to you, clear its primary name, and keep the name on an address you use in public. A name once set stays in the chain's history.
finding.x-name-record.title: Has a public name: {{name}}
gap.skipped: A check ran out of calls and did not run: {{check}}.
gap.truncated: The address is very active: only its newest transactions were read.
gap.unread: Not read yet: {{check}}. The page makes no call; Privacy score reads it.
